Megan —

Appreciate the quick read and the comments. Short answers up front:
• Pen test notice: we can be flexible but need to preserve a minimal ops lead time to schedule scoped testing and notify any impacted subsystems. I think 30 days is workable for standard hosted customers; 90 days was the conservative default for larger multi-tenant staging coordination.
• Evidence cadence: we typically offer the following baseline: quarterly SOC 2 artefact package (attestation, control matrix excerpts, and relevant logs), plus an ad-hoc evidence lane where we commit to providing requested items within 5 business days for non-sensitive artifacts and a negotiated window for items that require engineering pulls.

I'm looping in Kimberly (legal) to propose clean redline language for the exhibit and Ben (security/ops) to provide detail on staging access and ephemeral credentials for pen tests.

Proposed next steps:
1) Kimberly to propose exhibit language that accepts a 30-day pen-test notice with a short escalation carveout for multi-tenant customers.
2) Ben to attach a simple matrix that maps pen-test request -> evidence owner -> expected turnaround.
3) We share proposed redline + matrix by Wednesday; you confirm and we'll fold into the O/F.

If that timing works we can keep on the EOW target.

Best,

Megan / Soojin —

I've gone through the annotated exhibit and drafted targeted redline language (see excerpt below). I'm sending the excerpt inline so Procurement has a clear view before we share the full doc.

EXCERPT (proposed):
"Section 4.3 (Security Assessments): Customer may conduct a penetration test against Redwood systems that are within the agreed Scope of Testing, provided that Customer (i) provides Redwood with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice that includes the planned test window and target subsystems; (ii) follows Redwood's pen-test coordination runbook; and (iii) executes a nondisruptive testing plan. For customers requesting tests that require multi-tenant staging or elevated operational support, Redwood may request up to ninety (90) days' notice to coordinate resources; such request will be based on the complexity and potential impact and shall be documented in the Exhibit."

Evidence cadence (proposed exhibit paragraph):
"Redwood will provide a quarterly evidence package that includes SOC 2 attestation (when available), control mapping for relevant assertions, and pre-approved log extracts. For ad-hoc evidence requests, Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to respond within five (5) business days for non-sensitive items. Requests that require engineering-time or privileged data access will be subject to a mutually-agreed timeline documented in a joint action plan (JAP)."

Notes:
- The 30/90 split gives Healthbridge the shorter window you prefer while preserving the fallback for complex tests.
- We should attach Ben's matrix and a short one-page runbook to the exhibit so the operational expectations are explicit (who owns the evidence, what is in the quarterly bundle, staging-access guardrails).

I'll attach the full redline in Drive (linked below). If that looks acceptable to Healthbridge I can prepare a tracked-change version for inclusion in the Order Form.

Quick ops detail to support Kimberly's language and the exhibit:

I've attached the Pen Test Scope Matrix that maps typical requests to owners and turnaround bands. Highlights:
- Standard scoped tests (no privileged data, single-tenant staging) -> 30-day notice; ops lead assigned; evidence tasks 3-5 business days for log extracts.
- Elevated tests (multi-tenant staging, customer-supplied tooling, or forensic-level access) -> up to 90 days to schedule; engineering involvement; JAP required.

Runbook bullets (we'll attach a one-pager to the exhibit):
- Submit test request using the shared form -> include test window, targets, tools, point of contact.
- Redwood assigns ops lead and places the request in the pen-test queue.
- For ephemeral credentials, we provide timeboxed access with jump host and scoped session logs; customer must use provided sessions.

Megan — I'll upload the matrix and runbook to Drive and can join a short call if you want to walk through the operational steps.
